notes: [NO-EXTERNAL-EVIDENCE] — worklist hygiene only. No /data item is added, promoted, or edited by this batch; no verdict rests on any external page.

Diagnosis (measured 2026-07-29/30 against HEAD 97f4958): the held ledger showed 25 entries at session start, but 6 of them were not open work. apply-batch had exactly one exit from the worklist — `promotions[].to === 'reviewed'` — so a hold that ended in any other terminal disposition could never leave. Decisions (106) and (108) closed or parked 6 entries in 2026-07-03; all 6 kept surfacing at every session start since.

Two mechanisms added, both deliberate data rather than inference. (1) `held_resolutions` on the decision file closes a hold that ended in a non-promotion terminal disposition; apply-batch refuses a closure whose id is not on the worklist, so a typo cannot pass silently. (2) `recheck: 'trigger'` marks a hold whose blocking condition is an upstream event nobody here can act on; recheck-held renders those in their own group and reports open vs trigger-watch counts separately.

Why closure is stated and not inferred from status: of the 5 ledger entries whose item is now `deprecated`, only 2 are terminally over. The other 3 record live re-creation triggers, and a 4th trigger entry (subfield:modern-history) is parked at `proposed`, not deprecated at all. A status-derived rule would have dropped 3 live triggers and kept 1. The exact blocking_condition texts were re-read before this batch was authored rather than inferred from the roadmap's estimate ('6~8 already disposed'); the measured split is 2 closed / 4 trigger-watch / 19 open.

Blocking-condition prose for the 4 re-triaged entries is carried over verbatim from decisions (106)/(108) — only `recheck`, `batch_id`, `recorded_at` and `note` change. The audit trail stays in foundry/decisions/s12-holds-resolution-v1.json and weber-referent-precision-v1.json; held.json is a worklist, not the audit trail (§15.8).
